operational_caveats.search_success_telemetry_caveat: Matched V3 summary reports 164/165 search successes because task 0bdb7c40 threw an unhandled 403 exception during LLM generation, causing runner exception handler to default search_success=False. Tavily search was actually executed upon entry; the reported search failure is a metadata synthesis artifact of the subsequent LLM request exception.

scientific_conclusions.headline: Under the frozen V4 two-stage routing architecture, V4 solved 52/165 GAIA validation tasks (31.52%) versus 49/165 (29.70%) for the contemporaneous matched V3 control, an observed gain of 3 tasks (+1.82 percentage points). This gain coincided with a substantial reduction in completion from 77.58% to 49.70%.
scientific_conclusions.system_bundle_caveat: The V4 intervention bundles explicit routing, an additional model generation, route-specific prompting, deterministic route enforcement, and altered exposure to provider stochasticity; therefore the comparison does not isolate a pure causal effect of routing.
scientific_conclusions.successful_python_subset: On the endogenously selected 11-task subset where V4 Python execution succeeded, V4 solved 9 tasks and matched V3 solved 8. This is descriptive only and does not estimate a causal effect.
scientific_conclusions.matched_v3_final_task_sensitivity: The final matched V3 task experienced a control-side provider failure and is therefore an operational asymmetry/caveat. The same task was incorrect in V4, so the observed +3-task advantage is not created solely by this task. If matched V3 hypothetically solved this one task, the observed V4 advantage would decrease from +3 to +2 tasks rather than reverse direction.
